Hi all — quick write-up below you can forward to procurement/infosec. Happy to join a short call if you want to walk through.

1) Training-on-customer-data (opt-out by default)- Our default across Hosted and Dedicated is that we DO NOT use Customer Data to train or improve models for third-party distribution. Model training on customer-provided content only occurs when a customer explicitly opts in via contract (training_on_customer_data: opt-in).

Suggested contract language (short):
"Redwood will not use Customer Data (including transcripts, logs, or payloads) to train, improve, or derive models or model weights for any purpose other than providing the Service to Customer, nor will Redwood share Customer Data with model training pipelines for third-party models, unless Customer provides an explicit, written opt-in to such use."

2) Logs & transcripts- What is stored: Request metadata (timestamps, route, model), request/response IDs, and the request payload/transcript only when needed for debugging or as part of the Service (e.g., response storage for retrieval features). By default, raw request payloads and transcripts are persisted only if the customer enables persistence (e.g., to build conversation state). When persisted, we have redaction tools and tokenization options to remove PII.
- Default retention: 30 days for logs and transcripts on Hosted.
- Configurable retention: can be reduced to 7 days for pilots on Hosted; Dedicated and Private allow custom retention policies under contract.

3) PII handling & redaction- We recommend redaction at ingestion (customer-side) where possible. Additionally, our platform supports automatic redaction rules (PII masking) and configurable tokenization for sensitive fields. For high-sensitivity data, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment.

4) Data residency- Hosted: we can pin storage/region to US-only (us-west-2 / us-east-1) for the pilot; Dedicated: customer-dedicated pools can be restricted to a region or single AZ; Private: on-prem / VPC option for full residency control.

5) SOC2 & evidence- Attaching our SOC2 summary and Data Handling FAQ. For procurement, the suggested path is: 1) include the contract language above, 2) request SOC2 report under NDA if they need detailed evidence, 3) include the retention/residency cells in the SOW.

Attachment: SOC2-summary.pdf (application/pdf)

Please use the language above when sharing with procurement; happy to adapt wording if their legal team has edits.
